title: Strong user-presence approval class with platform verification
objective: Introduce the STRONG approval class on top of the SG-000018 replay-resistant foundation: PRIVILEGED and selected DESTRUCTIVE operations require platform-mediated local user-presence verification (Windows Hello style where feasible) instead of a soft button, with fail-closed denial where strong verification is unavailable, so the agent cannot produce a valid strong approval through its own tool or input surface.

include: SOFT versus STRONG approval class in the broker contract with STRONG bound to the existing nonce, expiry, one-shot, digest, workspace, and policy bindings
policy classification mapping PRIVILEGED operations and selected DESTRUCTIVE operations to the STRONG class while existing file, process, and Git operations retain their current class
platform user-presence verification boundary with capability detection and a testable provider seam
Windows Hello style verification path where feasible with fail-closed denial when strong verification is unavailable for STRONG-class operations
protected-surface enforcement during strong verification with input-lease suspension carried over from the existing approval boundary
approval history recording of class, presence result, and fallback denials without secret material
deterministic unit and security tests for class enforcement, unavailable-verification denial, presence forgery through agent surfaces, replay and drift retention, and separation
retention of all SG-000018 one-shot, expiry, digest, history, and P06 approval flows with no behavior change outside class enforcement
Windows and Ubuntu exact-head qualification with platform-specific verification tests gated to Windows
exclude: workspace trust creation, modification, or revocation
approval history UX beyond recorded class and presence fields
changes to per-operation digests, prompts, or summaries outside class labeling
new privileged capabilities or capability families
new network, browser, UI automation, clipboard, or installer authority
approval delegation to remote or MCP callers
synthetic-input generation or input injection of any kind

authority_delta.filesystem: No new filesystem writability beyond the existing approval history records, which gain class and presence fields.
authority_delta.process: No new process authority. Platform verification is a user-presence check mediated by the operating system, not process execution.
authority_delta.network: None. Presence verification is strictly local with no egress.
authority_delta.ui_input: None. No input injection is added; verification is accepted only through the platform-mediated presence result.
authority_delta.secrets: Presence results carry verification status only. Raw secrets and biometric material never enter prompts, records, history, logs, or audit.
authority_delta.approval: STRONG class requiring platform-mediated presence is added for PRIVILEGED and selected DESTRUCTIVE operations. SOFT behavior is unchanged. No persistent reuse or remote delegation is introduced.

invariants: PRIVILEGED and selected DESTRUCTIVE operations require STRONG approval and fail closed without verified presence
STRONG approval binds the full SG-000018 record: fresh nonce, exact digest, workspace, policy revision, short expiry, and one-shot consumption
A soft button alone never satisfies the STRONG class
The agent cannot produce a valid strong approval through MCP tools, synthetic input, UI automation, coordinates, or child processes
Presence verification is platform-mediated; Cotra never self-attests presence
Unavailable platform verification fails closed for STRONG-class operations without downgrading to SOFT
History records class and presence outcome without secret or biometric material
Existing SOFT flows keep exact digests, prompts, revalidation, and history behavior
No trust-change, reuse, delegation, browser, UI, network, or elevation authority is introduced

acceptance.claim: Tests prove the broker contract distinguishes SOFT and STRONG classes and binds STRONG to the existing nonce, expiry, one-shot, digest, workspace, and policy record.
Tests prove policy maps PRIVILEGED operations and selected DESTRUCTIVE operations to STRONG while existing file, process, and Git approvals retain their class.
Tests prove STRONG approval succeeds only with a platform-mediated presence result and fails closed when verification is unavailable, without SOFT downgrade.
Tests prove the agent cannot satisfy STRONG through MCP tools, synthetic input, UI automation, coordinate proposals, child processes, or replayed prior approvals.
Tests prove replay, expiry, digest mismatch, revision drift, and double-consumption protections from SG-000018 remain enforced for both classes.
Tests prove history records class and presence outcome with redaction and tamper-evident loading retained.
Tests prove denied and unavailable presence is recorded and never authorizes execution.
Tests prove all P06 approval flows still pass their regressions with digests unchanged.
Tests prove trust changes, persistent reuse, remote delegation, and broader process authority remain unreachable.
Windows-gated tests exercise the real platform verification path where feasible or record its unavailability explicitly without claiming unverified success.

Exact-head Windows/Ubuntu Rust, Node, Governance, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, exact-diff security review, manual review of excluded security-sensitive files, and zero unresolved blocking review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.trust_ux: Workspace trust management, approval history UX, and emergency revoke remain successor work and must build on the class-labeled history without weakening STRONG enforcement, one-shot, expiry, or digest binding.
successor_requirements.p07_exit: COTRA-P07 exits only when the agent cannot produce a valid strong approval through its own tool or input surface with replay and drift resistance proven, which this grain plus its trust-UX successor must jointly satisfy.

done_when: STRONG approval class with platform-mediated presence verification is merged for PRIVILEGED and selected DESTRUCTIVE operations with unavailable-verification denial, agent-forgery tests, retained SG-000018 replay and drift enforcement, class-labeled history, and no trust-change, reuse, delegation, or new platform authority.
